Revocation date and wording are right (EO 13990 Sec. 7(a), unqualified list, signed 2021-01-20; no saving clause). But the claim gives every Sec. 2 clause (2(a)-(c) review, 2(d) 45-day interim report, 2(e) 120-day final report) a first_end of 2021-01-20 by revocation. Read in full, Sec. 2 is a one-time review-and-report command; jobs/claim-kit/BATCH.md says 'A later revocation does not prove first cessation for a command already performed.' The review and reports were (per public record, not held) delivered in 2017, so the first cessation of the Sec. 2 clauses is the actual performance date, which no held source dates. The producer's earlier_end_check dismisses performance as 'not a legal ending'; that is contrary to the protocol. Correct outcome is blocked pending the report dates (reviewer added a FETCH_QUEUE request), or an applied-v4 that dates Sec. 2 by performance from a held source.

Confirmed EO 12553 list names 11049; ACTOR_TEXT-only and Public Works Acceleration Act expiry unexamined. FETCH_QUEUE line(s) match the gap

L. 94-412 sec. 101, 1978) and the end of the Commerce and Federal Reserve capital-transfer programs were not examined. The EO 11490 ACT records (1969) only reassign emergency-p Confirmed in EO 12553 list; emergency/program termination is the real first-cessation question. FETCH_QUEUE line(s) match the gap

Substance is plausible (clause 2 replaced 1951-04-26 when EO 10236 rewrote para 8 of EO 10129; the Commission then ceased at the end of 1951-05-31), but the claim as written is not defensible: (1) clause 1 and whole_order_end carry date 1951-05-31 with mechanism 'amend' and actor EO 10236, yet EO 10236 never amends paragraph 3 (the report date that clause 1 changed); clause 1 ended because the Commission ceased under the new para 8, which is a different mechanism; (2) the cited source quote (EO_10236.txt chars 1766-2336) stops at the opening quotation mark and does not contain 'The Commission shall cease to exist at the end of May 31,1951', so nothing quoted supports the 1951-05-31 date. The claim's own judgment_reason concedes this. A correction needs an end record whose span includes the cessation sentence (tooling gap: ACTOR_TEXT has no mechanism) and a fresh review.

Block justified: Evidence contradicts the provisional NO as a whole-order status. I read the complete held order (89 FR 60791-60792): Sec. 1 establishes the emergency board; Sec. 2 sets the 30-day report deadline; Sec. 3 imposes a 120-day status-quo duty; Sec. 5 terminates the Board on submission of its report (EO 14128 of 2024-11-21, held, recites that it did terminate, but not when). But Sec. 4 (Records Maintenance) says the Board's records 'are records of the Office of the President and upon the Board's termination shall be maintained in the physical custody of the National Mediation Board', a standing cust Agree unresolved: Sec. 4 custody direction has no stated end and the Board report date is not held. Read the held EO 10999 (27 FR 1527) and EO 11490 Sec. 3011-3015: item (7) of Sec. 3015 revokes 'Executive Order No. 10999 of February 16,1962' outright, signed 1969-10-28, no delayed effective wording found; Sec. 3014's retention is expressly subject to Sec. 3015. The 13-section inventory override is correct (neighbouring EO 10998/11000 excluded). Tried to refute: OFR catalog record for EO 10999 shows only 'Revoked by: EO 11490' plus 'See' cross-references (EO 10952; FR Doc. 62-9459, 27 FR 9418; FR Doc. 63-3328, 28 FR 3125) which are non-Presidential FR documents and cannot end a Presidential order; no amending EO in the catalog or held texts (grep of all held texts finds only incidental hits). Sec. 13's revocation of EP Order No. 2 was self-executing in 1962, but the same section's precedence sentence continued, so a 1969 first_end for the section is right and the executed part is correctly recorded as accrued. Savings transferred_or_accrued is right (EO 11490 Part 9 restates Commerce assignments). Minor: the producer did not name the 'See' cross-references; not outcome-changing.
